title: Admired Leaders Are a Rare Combination of Results and Followership
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Prompted by Linda Yaccarino's move to lead Twitter, this article explores the tension between results-driven leadership and relationship-driven leadership, arguing the two rarely coexist. Leaders who chase results with a hard edge often generate turnover and resistance even as they hit their numbers, while purely relational leaders may inspire loyalty without sustaining performance. The author argues that leaders who combine both qualities are exceptionally rare and are the ones who earn the label "Admired," closing with an open question about how Yaccarino's leadership style will play out.
points: Results-focused leaders often achieve strong outcomes but generate turnover through a hard-edged style.
Purely relational leaders inspire deep loyalty but may lack the discipline to sustain performance.
Leaders who combine both results and genuine followership are described as exceedingly rare.
The label "Admired" is reserved specifically for leaders who achieve both simultaneously.
quotes: Apparently, Yaccarino earned the label by combining a hard-nosed negotiation style with a warm and relational demeanor.
Identify an iconic leader with a well-known reputation and you will likely identify a results-based leader who has enjoyed tremendous success over many years.
Leaders who share both qualities—results and followership—are exceedingly rare and enjoy an unusual respect from almost everyone around them.
Team members refuse to let such leaders down, going above and beyond because they perceive a meaningful connection to the leader.
We have no idea if the “Velvet Hammer” is one such leader, but her reputation, at least to date, suggests she is operating in the right zip code.
